# Trump Discloses Up to $380,000 in Nvidia Buys, Calls Huang’s Exit ‘Such a Tragedy’

President **Donald Trump’s** portfolio bought between \$152,004 and \$380,000 in **Nvidia Corp.** [(NASDAQ:NVDA)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA) stock in September, according to an ethics disclosure released Thursday.

It sold up to \$15,000 on Sept. 24. That evening, Nvidia’s then-CEO **Jensen Huang** sat at the head table as Trump hosted Chinese President **Xi Jinping** at the White House.

Most of the [buying](https://extapps2.oge.gov/201/Presiden.nsf/PAS%2BIndex/20A6220DE9740AF085258EB400334364/$FILE/Donald-J-Trump-11.01.2026-278T%20optimized%20version.pdf) came in two trades on Sept. 2. The Nvidia sale was one of 109 trades the portfolio made on Sept. 24.

Those trades were small next to Trump’s overall Nvidia stake. The Washington Post [estimated](https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/11/16/trumps-stake-nvidia-grew-much-62-million-before-scandal-broke-out/) he held \$13 million to \$62 million in Nvidia at the end of August.

The White House said in October that outside firms manage the portfolio and track broad market indexes. It did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Reuters on Thursday.

### What Trump Said About Huang

By the time Trump and Xi dined again this week in Shenzhen, **Jensen Huang** had stepped down. Trump told Fox News he might have briefly mentioned Huang’s departure to Xi. He called it "such a tragedy."

Huang resigned Nov. 12 after reports of an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), the former CEO of Megaspeed. U.S. officials suspect she has ties to Chinese intelligence, The New York Times reported.

Trump said Monday he was open to Jensen Huang returning as CEO. Huang said Tuesday he’d come back if the board wanted him, but Nvidia’s directors said they had no plans to [reinstate](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/11/63374089/nvidia-board-rules-out-jensen-huang-return-despite-calls-for-ceo-comeback) him.

On Thursday, [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/jensen-huang-rejoins-nvidia-byptptpt/will-jensen-huang-rejoin-nvidia-by-december-31-2026) traders gave Jensen Huang a 5% chance of rejoining Nvidia by year-end. About \$3.28 million had traded on that deadline. A board seat or formal advisory role would also count.

### China’s Access to Nvidia Chips

Three House committees will [question](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/prediction-markets/26/11/63408059/altman-huang-comeback) Jensen Huang behind closed doors on Dec. 1 about how Chinese companies gained access to advanced Nvidia chips.

One company under scrutiny is Megaspeed, which Alice Huang used to run. It rents computing power to Chinese customers from data centers in Southeast Asia, the Associated Press [reported](https://apnews.com/article/nvidia-export-controls-chips-china-remote-access-60f868d3bb430b85a8657b27d421096e). U.S. authorities are [investigating](https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/joint-statement-department-commerce-and-department-justice-megaspeed-investigation) the company over possible export violations.

That’s the kind of remote access Washington tightened rules on Thursday. Some overseas data centers now need a [license](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-11-19/pdf/2026-23529.pdf) to give Chinese customers access to advanced U.S. chips.

Nvidia’s top lawyer, Tim Teter, is due to appear before the same committees the day after Huang.

# Anthropic Debut; New I Bonds Pay 5.51%; Intuit, Ross Stores and Gap After-Hours Earnings

Anthropic priced its initial public offering at \$83 a share on Wednesday, above the range it had marketed, according to CNBC, Bloomberg and Reuters. The reports landed after a split session on Wall Street: the S&P 500 fell for a fifth straight day while the Nasdaq Composite rose, and Federal Reserve officials talked openly about a larger interest rate increase.

#### MARKET SNAPSHOT

- **S&P 500** 7,323.63, down 0.2%
- **Nasdaq Composite** 24,429.88, up 0.4%
- **Dow** 50,198.17, down 1.1%
- **Russell 2000** 2,714.31, up 0.5%
- **10-year Treasury yield** 5.07%, from 5.10% on Tuesday
- **WTI crude** \$83.26, down 3.2%
- **Brent crude** \$91.95, down 1.3%
- **Gold** \$3,722.80, down 3.3%
- **Bitcoin** about \$62,300, down about 3%

*Closing levels for Wednesday, Nov 18, 2026. Oil is front-month futures. Gold is the spot price and Bitcoin the market price shortly before 5 p.m. ET.*

## Anthropic’s IPO priced at \$83, above its range

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI models, had marketed its shares at **\$70 to \$78**. On Wednesday afternoon CNBC, Bloomberg and Reuters each reported, citing people familiar with the deal, that the company settled on **\$83**. Anthropic had not announced the price itself as of early Wednesday evening.

The company’s latest filing listed **825 million shares** for sale. At \$83 that would raise about \$68.5 billion, by CNBC’s arithmetic. Bloomberg reported that the offering was also enlarged, so the final share count and the total raised are not confirmed. For scale, CNBC put SpaceX’s IPO in June at \$75 billion before extra shares were added.

Demand ran well ahead of supply. Orders came to nearly seven times the shares on offer, according to earlier reports, and up to 20% of the deal was set aside for individual investors through brokerages. An order is a request, and many investors receive fewer shares than they ask for, or none.

The stock is expected to start trading Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker **ANT**. Large IPOs usually open later in the morning, not at the 9:30 a.m. ET bell, and no time has been set.

> **Why it matters:** Anyone who owns AI stocks, including through index funds heavy in Nvidia, Amazon and Alphabet, gets a direct reading on Thursday of what public investors will pay for one of the companies at the center of the AI build-out. The IPO price is what large investors paid before trading began, and first-day prices in big offerings can swing sharply in either direction.

#### RATES

## Fed minutes show nearly every official expects to raise rates again

The Federal Reserve released the minutes of its Oct 27 to 28 meeting on Wednesday afternoon. Officials voted 10 to 2 at that meeting to hold the benchmark rate at **3.75% to 4.00%**, and the two dissenters wanted an increase. The minutes say "almost all participants" judged that further increases would likely be appropriate, and that "a couple" thought a move larger than a quarter point "could warrant consideration."

Hours earlier, Fed Governor Christopher Waller made the case for a bigger step in a CNBC interview.

> FED'S WALLER SAYS THE FED MAY NEED TO "SHOCK" PEOPLE\
> \
> Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he is very concerned that inflation is heading in the wrong direction and broadening, in a CNBC interview today.\
> \
> He said roughly 70% of the items in the core services basket are rising… [pic.twitter.com/VArE6RJBPb](https://t.co/VArE6RJBPb)
>
> — WOLF (@WOLF_Financial) [November 18, 2026](https://x.com/WOLF_Financial/status/2123037566492447186?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

The minutes also tie inflation to the AI boom. Fed staff called AI-related demand "a material source of inflation risk," according to CNBC’s account of the document. The next meeting is Dec 8 to 9. The dollar index, which tracks the dollar against other major currencies, reached a 19-month high.

> **Why it matters:** Borrowers feel a higher Fed rate first, through credit cards, car loans and adjustable-rate debt, while savers see it in higher yields on cash. Mortgage rates are already climbing: the average 30-year rate rose to 7.35% last week, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association.
>
> **Nvidia**
>
> ## Nvidia’s board says it will not bring Jensen Huang back, and the stock falls
>
> Nvidia shares opened higher on Wednesday after Tuesday night’s earnings beat, then reversed and closed at **\$150.96**, down 2.9%. It was the stock’s fifth straight decline. Other chipmakers rose, with AMD up 5.3% and Broadcom up 3.7%, which points to a company-specific worry.
>
> That worry is leadership. On the earnings call, Chair Harvey Jones answered the question that had been open since Huang said he would be honored to return.
>
> > Nvidia’s [\$NVDA](https://x.com/search?q=%24NVDA&src=ctag&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) chairman of the board of directors just said this:\
> > \
> > "Jensen Huang, voluntarily resigned his positions as President, CEO, and board member. The NVIDIA Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO" <https://t.co/qLL8BWzU8x>
> >
> > — Evan (@StockMKTNewz) [November 17, 2026](https://x.com/StockMKTNewz/status/2122813605431443499?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)
>
> Jones said the board has hired the search firm Heidrick & Struggles, will consider candidates from inside and outside the company, and will not rush the choice. He gave no timeline. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, the interim CEO, called it "business as usual" and closed the call with "We’ve got this." Management raised its outlook for revenue growth in its next fiscal year to about 75%, from 70%, CNBC reported.
>
> **Why it matters:** Nvidia is one of the heaviest weights in the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq, so index fund holders own it whether they picked it or not. Sales are still growing fast, and shareholders now face a CEO search with no end date at the company whose chips the AI industry depends on.
>
> MARKETS
>
> ## Health insurers sink the Dow while retailers rally
>
> The S&P 500’s fifth straight loss is its longest losing streak since June. The Dow fell **561 points**, and one stock did much of the damage: UnitedHealth dropped 10.2%. Humana fell 13.0%.
>
> Insurers sold off over a proposal from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to expand audits of Medicare Advantage plans, the private versions of Medicare, and to reclaim overpayments. The agency estimates about \$90 billion in savings over 10 years, according to press reports. The proposal is open for public comment and could change.
>
> Retailers went the other way after three earnings reports before the open:
>
> **Lowe’s** rose 1.0%. Its adjusted profit of \$3.10 a share included 34 cents from tariff refunds.
>
> **TJX**, the owner of T.J. Maxx and Marshalls, rose 8.0%. Sales at stores open at least a year grew 4%.
>
> **Target** rose 4.0% and raised its sales forecast for the year.

Tariff refunds lifted profit at all three retailers, a one-time help that says little about underlying demand. Energy was the weakest of the eleven sectors, down 3.2%, as crude fell on a larger-than-expected rise in US oil inventories.

**Why it matters:** A broad S&P 500 fund is now about 6% below its October record. Wednesday’s losses were concentrated in health insurers and energy and the gains in retailers and chipmakers outside Nvidia, so what an investor owns mattered more than the index move suggests.

#### QUICK HITS

- **Gold:** Spot gold fell below \$3,800 an ounce for the first time since September 2025 as the dollar strengthened on expectations of higher rates.
- **Housing:** Housing starts rose 9.9% in October from September. Building permits, a sign of future construction, fell 7.4% to their lowest level since May 2020.
- **Inflation abroad:** Consumer prices rose 3.6% from a year earlier in the UK in October, and the euro area’s rate was confirmed at 4.0%, with energy costs driving both.
- **Gas prices:** The national average for regular gas is \$3.75 a gallon, per AAA, down about 19 cents from a week ago.
- **Palo Alto Networks:** The cybersecurity company reported results after the close, raised its forecast for the year and agreed to buy AI startup Applied Compute for \$4.5 billion in stock.

#### MONEY NOTE

## New I bonds pay 5.51%

Series I savings bonds issued from November 2026 through April 2027 earn a combined rate of **5.51%**, according to TreasuryDirect. That is a fixed rate of 1.40% that lasts for the life of the bond, plus an inflation rate that resets every six months. I bonds cannot be cashed in during the first 12 months, and cashing in before five years gives up the last three months of interest.

- **Digital Assets**: Bitcoin steadied near USD 63,000 while Strategy led crypto shares lower and funds bled

## **Macro**

- **Minutes of the October Fed meeting showed nearly all officials agreed further rate increases would likely be needed** in the months ahead, and Governor Waller said a half-point hike should be considered at the December meeting, citing core inflation running near 3.5% annualised over three months. The market has by now priced in three more increases, taking the policy rate to 4.50% to 4.75% by June 2027.
- **US housing starts rose 9.9% in October** to an annualised 1.309 million, above the 1.250 million expected, while building permits fell 7.4% to 1.295 million against 1.375 million expected, a reading seen as signalling a weaker pipeline. UK inflation rose to a one-year high of 3.6% in October from 3.5% in September, with transport and motor fuel costs the main contributors.
- **Geopolitics:** President Trump signalled that Ukraine will feature in today's trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, following an earlier meeting with Putin that reportedly ended on a positive note. Trump also praised his relationship with Xi and downplayed the Nvidia spying controversy. Meanwhile, tensions with Iran remain elevated, with the New York Times reporting that Trump is considering fresh military strikes amid indications Tehran is rebuilding its missile stockpile.

Reports of a technical disruption to the NSA's network coincided with a safe-haven bid for Treasuries and the yen on Tuesday.

## **Equities**

- **USA**: The S&P 500 fell 0.2% for a fifth consecutive decline and the Dow lost 1.1%, while the Nasdaq 100 rose 0.4% as technology proved more resilient. Federal Reserve minutes reinforced concerns over further interest-rate increases, while Nvidia dropped 2.9% despite strong earnings and guidance, as investors continued to question its leadership transition. UnitedHealth sank 10.2% after proposed tighter Medicare Advantage audits, while TJX gained 8.1% following strong sales and an improved outlook. Palo Alto Networks added almost 10% during regular trading and rose further after hours following upbeat results, ahead of Anthropic's market debut.
- **Europe**: The Stoxx 600 fell 1% for a third consecutive session, while the DAX lost 1.2%, the FTSE 100 declined 1.3% and the CAC 40 slipped 0.9% as falling commodity prices weighed on sentiment. Mining stocks dropped 4.7% as copper hit a seven-month low, pulling Antofagasta down 7.9%, while Glencore lost more than 5%. SAP fell 3.8% amid renewed pressure on software stocks, while ASML gained 1.9% as Nvidia's strong revenue outlook supported chip equipment suppliers. Elsewhere, Alstom dropped 7.2% after reporting a net loss, adding to concerns over corporate earnings.
- **Asia**: Asian equities traded mixed on Thursday, with Hong Kong’s Hang Seng down 1.9%, Japan’s Nikkei 225 rising 0.7% and South Korea’s Kospi fluctuating, while Australia’s ASX 200 closed down 1%. Hong Kong technology stocks led the retreat as Tencent fell 7% in afternoon trading after disappointing revenue growth and rising artificial intelligence spending raised concerns over profitability, while Alibaba weakened ahead of its earnings. In Australia, BHP dropped 3.7% and Rio Tinto lost 4.1% as copper prices slumped, while Japanese technology stocks helped offset weakness in banks and metals. Investors awaited Alibaba’s results and Japan’s inflation figures for further direction.

- Investors grew a little calmer on Wednesday, but they are not yet treating this week's selloff as over. The VIX eased to 24.56 after jumping about seven points in a week, and **demand for one-day protection fell sharply**. Futures tell a more reassuring story: **traders expect the fear to fade by December**, with later months priced below today's level and barely rising beyond that.
- The 9 December Fed meeting, where **a half-point hike is now openly discussed**, is the next big test. Options price a move of about 1.12% for today, with Walmart and Alibaba results ahead. Volatility in the bond market also eased, backing the calmer tone.

- Bitcoin steadied near **USD 63,000** after losing about 12% in a week. Traders being forced out of leveraged bets made the drop worse. Shares in crypto companies fell harder than the coins. **Strategy lost 6.40%** as investors questioned its habit of selling new shares to buy back its preferred stock, with bitcoin now well below the average price the company paid. Riot went the other way, rising almost 7%.
- **Bitcoin funds lost about USD 306m** on Wednesday, almost half of it from BlackRock's IBIT. Wells Fargo's filing, though, showed it more than doubled its IBIT holding last quarter. Sentiment sits at extreme fear.

## **Commodities**

- **Copper slumped 5% yesterday to a seven-month low**, pressured by global growth concerns, disappointing Chinese demand signals and expectations of increased US exports. Negative sentiment at a major industry conference in Shanghai triggered heavy speculative selling, while reports that more than 100,000 tonnes of copper could be redirected to China in December eased concerns about tight local supplies. Despite the sharp selloff, the longer-term outlook remains supported by tight scrap and mine supplies, resilient infrastructure demand and committed AI-related investment.
- **Precious metals**: Gold extended its recent slump, touching a fresh 15-month low of USD 3,694 in Asia, as hawkish Fed minutes and Governor Waller's comments reinforced expectations of further rate hikes. Beyond higher yields and rate hike concerns, the broader commodity selloff may also reflect tightening global dollar liquidity as the dollar continues to rally. Rising AI-related financing needs, IPO activity, equity market volatility and elevated energy security costs are increasing demand for cash just as higher interest rates make funding more expensive. Gold, given its deep liquidity, and other metals may therefore be caught in a broader *dash for cash*, with investors selling liquid assets to meet funding needs and reduce risk exposure.
- **Oil**: Brent trades near unchanged around USD 92 after falling 1.3% on the Wednesday. Alongside broader risk reduction across commodities, recent weakness has been driven by recovering Middle East production and exports, renewing concerns about an emerging supply glut. However, the risk of fresh disruptions remains, with the New York Times reporting that Trump, under renewed pressure from Israel's Netanyahu, is considering fresh strikes against Iran. ---

## **Fixed Income**

- **US Treasury yields edged a bit lower at the long end of the curve, while short-date yields remained rangebound.** The benchmark 2-year treasury yield traded little changed near 4.80% While the benchmark 10-year treasury yield moved four basis points lower Wednesday to close near 5.07% and was even down close to 5.05% in early Thursday trading. A US Treasury auction of 20-year notes saw demand in the middle of the range of prior auctions, which was better than the demand metrics at recent 10-year and 30-year treasury auctions.
- **Japan’s 20-year JGB auction:** Demand was notably weak, with a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.64 versus 5.84 at the prior auction and a 12-month average of 3.92, reflecting reduced appetite for long-duration amid rising inflation and rate expectations.

---

## **Currencies**

- **The US dollar remains strong, pulling to new highs for the cycle against a weak AUD** (more on that below) and CAD, while elsewhere price action was muted. **EURUSD** probed almost to 1.0950 in a new low since early 2025 Wednesday, but rebounded slightly by early Thursday. **GBPUSD** was slightly weaker than EURUSD on relative GBP softness and extended its range beyond the 2026 lows of 1.3136, where it trades early Thursday. The JPY’s relative strength faded overnight into early Thursday as **USDJPY** rebounded above 159.50 after a low of 159.13 Wednesday,
- **AUD was hit by a weak October jobs report and the spike in the unemployment rate to 4.9%**, sending AUD to the lowest levels since the first week of 2026 below 0.6665. AUDNZD fell to a new local low below 1.2140 before rebounding slightly. AUD sentiment has also been hit by the weakness in copper prices.

I'm going through the macro backdrop now: the Fed funds rate sits at 3.75–4.00%, with markets pricing about three more hikes by mid-2027, and a 25 or 50bp move being discussed for December 9. Core inflation is running around 3.5% annualised over three months, euro-area inflation is at 4.0%, the dollar is rallying, and USDJPY is near 159.5.

I'm checking the oil and geopolitical picture next: Brent around $92 after a prior Middle East disruption, with Trump weighing fresh strikes on Iran. I'm also weighing Taiwan tensions, TSMC's tighter China chip rules, Nvidia's leadership and export problems, and the AI-spending selloff with Bitcoin down 12% this week. Then I'm mapping the portfolio's exposure to rates and these sectors, since the bond holdings and Fed path matter most for the December 9 decision.

I'm weighing the December 9 Fed decision along with the longer rate path, since both BND and TLT are rate-sensitive and the 10-year yield could push past 5.5%. I'm also looking at Nvidia's CEO situation and export-control risk, given its 6.7% weight, and at whether hyperscaler capex cuts in early 2027 would hit the AI exposure.

I'm working through the remaining event risks for the portfolio: a hyperscaler cutting 2027 capex would hit the semis exposure, which is about 14.6%. A Taiwan blockade or shift in US policy would matter most for TSM and anything depending on TSMC, and a US strike on Iran could push Brent above $110 or below $75, helping XOM while pressuring the rest. I'm also considering a 20% S&P drawdown as a broader recession scenario.

I'm now checking Apple, the portfolio's largest holding at 8.3%, including any recent filings and whether a CEO transition is underway. I'm also going through the risks that could move it: Q1 earnings, semiconductor tariffs, antitrust, and memory cost pressure on margins. Then I'll turn to Microsoft at 6.9%.

I'm going through the remaining holdings now, starting with Microsoft's upcoming late-January earnings and its OpenAI relationship. Then I'm checking Jamie Dimon's succession and the vendor cyberattack risk at JPMorgan, along with the mid-January earnings date. I'm also looking at Novo Nordisk's drug pipeline and pricing pressures, and how the yen near 159.5 and auto tariffs could affect Toyota.

I'm checking Bitcoin next, with IBIT at 2.4% and Bitcoin near $63k amid extreme fear, and whether forced selling could push it below $50k. Then I'm looking at the dollar's strength against the foreign holdings, and the tariff picture, including Supreme Court refunds and Section 232 on semiconductors. I'm also weighing the US political backdrop after the November midterms, the funding and debt-ceiling deadlines, and who the next Fed chair is.

I'm narrowing the list of event risks to the ones that matter most by weight, since there are too many to track evenly. I'll look at markets and company filings for the main ones before settling on a short list of about ten to twelve.

# Tech Stocks Wipe Out $960 Billion as Washington Shuts China's AI Chip Back Door in 5 Countries

For years, Chinese companies did not need to smuggle [America’s most powerful AI chips](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/11/63290031/nvidia-jensen-huang-profumo-espionage-risk-adam-irwin-heligan). A rented server in Southeast Asia was enough.

On Monday, Washington moved to lock that door, and the bill landed on Wall Street.

The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule that requires a license to ship advanced AI chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. Washington says these five countries “present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

By 2:40 p.m. ET, 19 of the largest U.S.-listed technology stocks had lost about \$960 billion in combined market value.

**Nvidia Corp.** [(NASDAQ:NVDA)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA) took the biggest hit. The stock fell 4.4% to \$155.70, erasing roughly \$172 billion in its first full week without **Jensen Huang** at the helm.

The **VanEck Semiconductor ETF** [(NASDAQ:SMH)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SMH) slid 4.7%. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 2.4% and the S&P 500 fell 1.9%.

**Read Also: [EXCLUSIVE: Huang's Exit Echoes Profumo, but Intelligence Expert Says Chip CEOs Are the New Spy Targets](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/11/63290031/nvidia-jensen-huang-profumo-espionage-risk-adam-irwin-heligan)**

## **How the Cloud Back Door Worked**

Since 2022, Chinese companies have largely been barred from buying Nvidia’s most advanced chips.

Renting them was a different story. Data centers in Southeast Asia could buy the hardware legally and then sell the computing power to customers in China, who never had to touch a single chip.

The new rule bars shipments to any data center, anywhere in the world, that gives companies headquartered in China, Macau or other arms-embargoed countries access to more than 12 million units of “aggregate TPP.”

Total processing performance is the yardstick Washington uses to measure raw computing power.

Data centers that already serve those customers have 90 days to obtain a license. Operators are also expected to check who ultimately owns their clients, and a customer that refuses to answer is treated as a red flag.

“The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries,” the Bureau of Industry and Security said in a statement.

## **Treasury Turns on Commerce**

The rule landed three days after Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** took a fight inside the administration public.

Nvidia’s board accepted **Jensen Huang**‘s resignation on Nov. 11, after he admitted to an affair with **Alice Huang**, a former executive at Singapore-based data center company **Megaspeed** whom U.S. officials are still investigating over whether she is a Chinese intelligence asset.

Bessent said four agencies had wanted Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist for months.

“Treasury, War, USTR, and State, they were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months,” Bessent said Friday. “But Commerce has the pen, Commerce BIS has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes.”

The Bureau of Industry and Security, the agency that wrote Monday’s rule, sits inside **Howard Lutnick**‘s Commerce Department.

On Sunday, Bessent turned to Nvidia itself.

“They need a dramatic shake-up,” he said.

He also urged the board to look past internal candidates. “This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader, that they need to go outside the company,” Bessent said.

The White House has said President **Donald Trump** “maintains complete confidence” in Lutnick, who has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee.

Bank of America had seen this coming.

“The Nvidia gate opens a can of worms that goes beyond the immediate pressure on the stock market,” Bank of America global economists **Claudio Irigoyen** and **Antonio Gabriel** said in a report Monday.

“Jensen Huang’s departure will likely trigger heightened geopolitical tensions between the US and China, and an eventual motion for tighter export controls across chips and rare earths,” they added.

**Read Also: [Nvidia Gets 10 Bank Downgrades After Huang Exit: What to Expect Ahead of Q3 Results](https://www.benzinga.com/analyst-stock-ratings/downgrades/26/11/63290113/nvidia-downgrades-huang-exit-third-quarter-earnings-preview)**

## **Even the Exempt Got Hit**

On paper, America’s cloud giants are spared. The license requirement for the five countries does not apply to customers headquartered in the United States, as long as exporters file the new reports the rule requires.

Investors sold them anyway.

**Alphabet Inc.** [(NASDAQ:GOOGL)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GOOGL) fell 3.8%, losing about \$135 billion, while **Amazon.com Inc.** [(NASDAQ:AMZN)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AMZN) shed 3.5%, or roughly \$101 billion.

# TSMC Slumps Nearly 6% as Jensen Huang’s Exit and AI Debt Fears Rattle Investors Ahead of Nvidia Earnings

Six days after reporting record monthly sales, **Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.** [(NYSE:TSM)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TSM) lost about \$106 billion in market value in Taipei on Monday.

**Nvidia Corp.** [(NASDAQ:NVDA)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA) holds its first earnings call since **Jensen Huang** resigned on Tuesday. Investors will be listening for whether Nvidia will keep helping customers finance their chip purchases.

If buyers take longer to raise money, chip orders could slip. Nvidia is TSMC’s biggest customer and accounts for an estimated 22% of its 2026 sales, according to JPMorgan Asia Pacific Equity [Research](https://am.jpmorgan.com/content/dam/jpm-am-aem/global/en/insights/eye-on-the-market/ai-tracker-amv.pdf).

TSMC shares opened slightly lower in Taiwan on Monday and ended the day down nearly 6%. Foxconn and MediaTek fell even more. Local dealers said Friday’s U.S. tech selloff spilled into Taiwan as investors weighed Nvidia’s future.

### Kress Had Already Pushed Back on Huang’s Deals

At a meeting in Berlin last month, Huang told cloud executives that if they wanted Nvidia chips, they’d need to get customers to pay in advance for the computing power they planned to rent out, The Wall Street Journal [reported](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/nvidias-days-as-an-open-checkbook-for-the-ai-economy-are-numbered-90c7b388).

As Nvidia’s finance chief, **Colette Kress** had already questioned how much the company stood to earn from guaranteeing customers’ data center deals. Over the summer, she reworked a deal to back an OpenAI data center in Ohio, cutting Nvidia’s proposed commitment roughly in half, the Journal [reported](https://www.wsj.com/tech/jensen-huang-colette-kress-nvidia-ceo-eb289097).

Apollo and Blackstone are still discussing deals under Nvidia’s August plan to raise more than \$500 billion from outside investors, according to Reuters. Huang said Nvidia could back up to \$125 billion under that plan.

On Tuesday, Kress will have her first chance as interim CEO to tell investors whether Nvidia is willing to put its own money behind it’s customers orders.

### Huang May Not Be Gone for Good

Huang has discussed a comeback with confidants, the Financial Times [reported](https://www.ft.com/content/45383d86-33c4-4d99-86e5-5e058d3567c1). If he returned as CEO, the man who built the financing plan would be setting its terms again.

[Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/jensen-huang-rejoins-nvidia-byptptpt/will-jensen-huang-rejoin-nvidia-by-december-31-2026) gave him about a 14% chance Monday of an announced return in any formal role by year-end, with \$1.15 million traded on that contract. A board seat would count, so the odds of him running Nvidia again are lower.

Analysts [expect Nvidia’s third-quarter](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/11/63282757/nvidia-must-now-prove-its-bigger-than-jensen-huang) revenue to reach about \$109 billion, but that quarter closed with Huang still in charge. What TSMC investors need is the outlook, and a sense of which buyers Nvidia will still back.

In October, TSMC CEO **C.C. Wei** said the company sends its own teams to U.S. data centers to check on construction and power. Their verdict was "so far so good."

That was before Huang resigned. At 5 p.m. ET Tuesday, interim CEO Colette Kress gives investors their first read since.

# No Jensen, No Problem? NVIDIA Delivers Strong Outlook, Rules Out Huang’s Return

**NVIDIA Corp.** [](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA)[(NASDAQ:NVDA)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA) stock rose nearly 4% in Wednesday’s premarket session as investors reacted to stronger-than-expected quarterly results and an [upbeat growth outlook](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/11/63372441/nvidia-stock-jumps-on-q3-double-beat-strong-outlook-explosive-demand-for-vera-rubin).

A broader recovery in technology stocks also supported the gains. Nasdaq futures rose 0.94%, while S&P 500 futures gained 0.46%.

The chipmaker’s quarterly results and strong artificial intelligence demand helped ease concerns about its near-term performance.

However, NVIDIA continues to face leadership uncertainty and regulatory scrutiny. Investors are weighing the company’s growth prospects against succession, China exposure [and financing risks](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/11/63356810/why-nvidia-is-falling-tuesday-jensen-huangs-comeback-statement-congress-hearings-and-ai-risks).

## Kress Seen As Steady Interim Leader

**D.A. Davidson** Managing Director **Gil Luria** [told](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/18/arms-rene-haas-leads-nvidia-ceo-race-but-company-ties-could-be-hurdle.html) CNBC on Wednesday that interim CEO **Colette Kress** can guide NVIDIA through the transition because she knows the business well. Still, he does not view her or other insiders as ideal permanent candidates while investigations into Asian sales continue.

Luria called **Arm Holdings Plc** [](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ARM)[(NASDAQ:ARM)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ARM) CEO **Rene Haas** the leading external candidate because of his semiconductor experience and familiarity with NVIDIA, while also naming **Apple Inc.** [](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AAPL)[(NASDAQ:AAPL)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AAPL) hardware chief **Johny Srouji** and **Broadcom Inc.** [](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AVGO)[(NASDAQ:AVGO)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AVGO) executive **Charlie Kawwas** as potential alternatives.

**Futurum** analyst **Rolf Bulk** [also](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/18/nvidia-transition-chip-development-create-openings-for-rivals-futurum.html) described Haas as a top contender. However, he said NVIDIA would still need to reorganize reporting lines and rebuild some of the relationships Huang personally managed.

## Strong Results Ease Near-Term Demand Concerns

After NVIDIA’s quarterly report, Luria said demand remained strong enough for the company to raise its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to 75% from 70%, even as it acknowledged uncertainty around Asian sales.

**Susquehanna** analyst **Chris Rolland** called the quarter a “very solid report” and [told](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/nvidia-out-with-very-solid-report-says-susquehannas-chris-rolland.html) CNBC that Kress and board chair **Harvey Jones** were doing a strong job establishing stability.

**Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster** [told](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/sec-investigation-an-expected-outcome-for-nvidia-says-deepwaters-gene-munster.html) CNBC that he viewed NVIDIA’s decision to guide as particularly bullish because Kress put her name behind the outlook despite the leadership turmoil and new export restrictions.

**StoneX** analyst **Cody Acree** [also](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/nvidia-board-will-likely-stick-to-decision-regarding-jensen-huang-says-stonexs-cody-acree.html) described the results as solid across revenue, guidance and gross margin.

**See More: [Top Value Stocks](https://www.benzinga.com/screener/top-value-stocks)**

## Kress Says Demand And Supply Remain Strong

Kress told CNBC that customer demand for NVIDIA’s computing infrastructure continues to rise and that expanded supply across chips, advanced packaging and memory supported the higher growth forecast.

She also rejected concerns about a widespread employee exodus, saying leadership and staff remain focused on executing the company’s roadmap.

Kress [told](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/watch-jim-cramers-full-interview-with-nvidia-interim-ceo-colette-kress.html) CNBC that NVIDIA plans to continue stock repurchases, with \$277 billion available, while maintaining disciplined investments across the AI ecosystem.

## Financing Strategy May Become More Selective

Bulk expects NVIDIA to scrutinize new neocloud financing deals more closely while continuing to support existing customers such as **CoreWeave** **Inc.** [](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CRWV)[(NASDAQ:CRWV)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CRWV) and **OpenAI**.

Before the results, **Cantor Fitzgerald** analyst **C.J. Muse** [told](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/cantor-fitzgeraldas-cj-muse-on-nvidia-interim-ceo-kress-likely-to-reiterate-70-percent-growth-for-2027.html) CNBC on Tuesday that he expected NVIDIA to temper its investment levels, potentially forcing some neocloud partners to seek more outside financing.

However, Rolland said NVIDIA’s post-earnings disclosures suggested the company was still “leaning into” financing commitments rather than withdrawing broadly.

## Huang Return Appears Unlikely

Former CEO **Jensen Huang** said he would be willing to return if NVIDIA’s board asked him to, but Kress said the board “will not reinstate Jensen.”

Rolland also said he does not expect Huang to return as CEO, though he believes NVIDIA could benefit from using him as an outside strategic or technical adviser.

**Wolfe Research** analyst **Chris Caso**, in a CNBC [interview](https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/11/17/jensen-huang-faces-tough-road-if-he-returns-to-nvidia-wolfe-researchs-caso.html) on Tuesday, similarly described Huang’s path back as difficult, given precedent involving CEOs and relationships with employees.

## Investigations Remain A Major Overhang

NVIDIA continues to face scrutiny over sales through Asia and potential access to restricted chips.

Luria estimates that 5% to 20% of NVIDIA chip sales may have reached China directly or through resellers and Asian data centers, which drove his price-target reduction to \$200 from \$300, despite maintaining a Buy rating.

Munster called the reported SEC investigation an “expected outcome” of the turmoil and said the central financial risk is whether tighter Asian restrictions reduce revenue.

Despite those concerns, analysts broadly viewed NVIDIA’s underlying demand and product roadmap as resilient.

# Nvidia’s $500 Billion Financing Plan Has Yet to Put a Dollar to Work, WSJ Reports

Six Wall Street firms signed on to a \$500 billion plan in August to help customers buy chips from **Nvidia Corp.** [(NASDAQ:NVDA)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA). Three months later, the plan has yet to put any money to work, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Some lenders want a bigger guarantee from Nvidia in case a customer defaults and the chips sell for less than expected, the [Journal](https://www.wsj.com/finance/wall-street-pledged-to-mobilize-500-billion-for-nvidiabut-hasnt-put-up-a-dime-1e41f276) reported.

**Jensen Huang**, who pushed for the plan, [resigned last week](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/11/63186620/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns-cfo-collette-kress-in-as-interim-ceo). His interim replacement, **Colette Kress**, had already questioned some of those guarantees as CFO.

Huang had envisioned a \$1 trillion partnership. At the August launch, **Goldman Sachs** CEO **David Solomon** [said](https://www.apollo.com/insights-news/pressreleases/2026/08/nvidia-partners-with-apollo) the industry was in a "pivotal moment of a historic AI investment cycle." The six firms had no obligation to raise the money, the Journal reported.

Two of those firms had already done a deal involving Nvidia’s rival. In June, **Apollo** [(NYSE:APO)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/APO) and **Blackstone** helped arrange \$35 billion for **Anthropic** to deploy chips from **Broadcom Inc.** [(NASDAQ:AVGO)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AVGO). The deal frustrated Huang and pushed him to speed up his own effort, the Journal reported.

### Who Takes the Loss?

In August, Huang [said](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-ai-factory-compute/) Nvidia might protect lenders against weak resale prices on up to 25% of a deal. Broadcom had agreed to a much bigger guarantee, covering about 85% of the Anthropic financing, the Journal reported.

On Tuesday’s [Nvidia earnings call](https://www.benzinga.com/content/63374236/nvidia-q3-2027-earnings-call-transcript), Kress said the company would be selective about the deals it backs. Apollo CEO **Marc Rowan** told CNBC that if Nvidia stopped acting as guarantor, "access to capital for a large number of neoclouds is going to disappear." Those companies buy chips and rent out the computing power.

### What Happens if Chip Rents Fall?

If those companies earn less from renting out chips, the chips could also fetch less on resale. That could leave Nvidia with a bigger bill if a customer defaults on a deal it guaranteed.

A sharp drop in Nvidia H100 rents is one of six triggers in [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/ai-bubble-burst-by/ai-industry-downturn-by-december-31-2026-857)’s AI-bubble market. Silicon Data’s H100 rental [index](https://www.silicondata.com/products/silicon-index/h100) was at \$3.01 per GPU-hour on Nov. 18. It would have to fall by about two-thirds, to \$1 or less, and stay there for five straight days to count.

The contract requires three of the six triggers within 90 days. Traders put the odds at 8% by year-end and 19% by June 30, 2027, with \$3.93 million traded across deadlines.

People familiar with the talks told the Journal they expect the first deal in 2027 at the earliest. Its terms will show how much of the risk lenders can persuade Nvidia to take.

# Gavin Newsom Calls Trump ‘Wholly Owned Subsidiary of Big Oil’ as Iran Tensions Rattle Oil Markets: Says President’s ‘Head Is Stuck in Sand Soaked With Oil’

Gov. **Gavin Newsom** (D-CA) slammed President **Donald Trump** and the White House’s pro-fossil fuel stance amid heightened energy costs and tensions between Washington and Tehran during the ongoing war.

## Trump Is a ‘Wholly-Owned’ Subsidiary, Says Gavin Newsom

In a post on the social media platform **X** on Thursday, Newsom shared a clip of his appearance at the COP31 conference in Türkiye. “Donald Trump’s head is stuck in sand soaked with oil,” the California governor said in the post. “He’s a wholly owned subsidiary of Big Oil,” Newsom said.

He also criticized Trump’s “aggressive assaults” on climate leadership with his policies. “California will continue to dominate with a low carbon, green growth economy that can’t be held hostage by foreign wars or Big Oil’s greed,” Newsom said.

> After softening the tone previously in regards to escalation, this certainly is not moving the needle in the right direction
>
> — Patrick De Haan (@GasBuddyGuy) [November 12, 2026](https://x.com/GasBuddyGuy/status/2120869385212416157?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Notably, Iran’s top security official, **Mohsen Rezaee**, had earlier warned the U.S. [against carrying out fresh strikes](https://www.benzinga.com/news/politics/26/11/63173398/oil-prices-rise-as-iran-threatens-us-bases-across-europe-and-middle-east-if-trump-launches-fresh-strikes-no-safe-distance-no-safe-haven-no-immunity) against Iran, saying that the move could result in lethal strikes on U.S. bases across the Middle East and Europe, which will become “legitimate targets” for Tehran.

## Oil, Gas Movement

Gas prices fell further as the American Automobile Association (AAA) [data](https://gasprices.aaa.com/) showed the national average price of gas on Thursday to \$3.9082/gallon. Diesel prices also fell on Wednesday, with the national average at \$6.0977/gallon.

At press time, the **West Texas Intermediate** (WTI) futures expiring in December were down 0.07% to \$88.68. On the other hand, **Brent** futures contracts expiring in January gained 0.50% to \$96.30 at the time of writing this article.

The **ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/UCO)[UCO](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/UCO)) was down 0.37% to \$53.50 during overnight trading on Thursday. The **United States Oil Fund** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/USO)[USO](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/USO)) ETF slipped 0.14% to \$145.87 during overnight trading.

## Ron DeSantis Criticizes Pro-Climate Stance

Gov. **Ron DeSantis** (R-FL) delivered sharp criticism of Democratic Party lawmakers as the GOP incurred setbacks in the midterm elections earlier this month after Former Secretary of State **John Kerry** said that voters had chosen to vote for a pro-climate stance in the midterms. DeSantis warned that [cutting oil production will not reduce costs](https://www.benzinga.com/news/politics/26/11/63174327/ron-desantis-says-stifling-oil-and-gas-production-will-not-lower-high-energy-prices-as-former-obama-official-pushes-climate-policy).

[(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XOM)[XOM](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XOM)) and **ConocoPhillips** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/COP)[COP](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/COP)) saw a slight uptick in overnight trading on Thursday. CVX shares were up 0.53% to \$217.50. Meanwhile, COP shares also gained 0.16% to \$140.29. XOM was up 0.34% to \$170.35 during overnight trading.

# CPI Inflation Beats Projections, Bitcoin Holds at $74,000 as ETH, XRP Stay Flat

**Bitcoin** [(CRYPTO: BTC)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BTC-USD), **Ethereum** [(CRYPTO: ETH)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ETH-USD) and **XRP** [(CRYPTO: XRP)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XRP-USD) traded sideways after October CPI came in hotter than expected, strengthening the case for another Fed rate hike.

### October CPI Comes In Hotter Than Expected

Headline CPI rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast, while core CPI climbed 0.3% versus the 0.2% economists expected, [as reported](https://x.com/DeItaone/status/2120147296587251740) by Bloomberg.

Here’s how October’s price increases broke down by category:

- Food: +0.5%
- Energy: +0.7%
- Gasoline: +1.0%
- Housing: +0.3%
- Real earnings (private sector): flat

Core inflation accelerated to 3.7% annualized over the past three months, its highest reading since January 2025, Walter Bloomberg flagged separately. Supercore inflation, which strips out housing and food, surged to 5.5% annualized, the fastest pace since April 2024 and up sharply from September’s 4.6%.

The six-month core CPI rate actually eased to 2.7% from 2.9%, though an unofficial estimate pegs annual core inflation at 2.74%, up from 2.56% previously.

### Bitcoin and XRP ETFs Keep Bleeding Outflows

Spot Bitcoin ETFs logged \$201 million in net outflows Monday, extending BlackRock’s [(NASDAQ:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IBIT)[IBIT](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IBIT)) to a seventh straight losing session with \$213.2 million pulled from that fund alone. 

That follows a broader weekly withdrawal of \$1.28 billion that flipped Bitcoin ETF flows negative for all of 2026, now sitting at \$914 million in net outflows for the year.

U.S. spot XRP ETFs lost \$10.42 million on Nov. 9, [according to SoSoValue](https://sosovalue.com/assets/etf/us-xrp-spot) data, ending four straight trading days with no flows at all and marking the largest single-day outflow since March 9’s \$18.11 million withdrawal.

### Where BTC, ETH and XRP Stand Technically

Bitcoin trades below \$75,000 and all four major EMAs, with RSI near 34 signaling weak momentum. 

Further support sits around \$73,500, then \$72,000, while resistance lies at \$75,000 to \$76,400.

Meanwhile, Ethereum trades around \$2,060, extending its decline below all four major EMAs, with RSI near 30 approaching oversold territory. 

Support sits at \$2,030 to \$2,000, then \$1,900, while recovery faces resistance at \$2,130 to \$2,200.

XRP is down to \$1.06, trading well below its major EMAs, with RSI near 24 signaling oversold conditions that haven’t yet confirmed a reversal. 

Support lies at \$1.05, then \$1, while resistance sits at \$1.10, then \$1.22.

# Nvidia—Wall Street Is Missing China-Linked Margin Risk—Buybacks Support Stock

![](https://thearorareport.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/NVDA-Chart-2026-11-18_08h16_07.jpg)

#### **Wall Street Misses NVDA’s Margin Risk**

Please click [here](https://thearorareport.com/stock-market-chart-analysis-nvidia-margins-earnings-china-money-flows-mc-18) for an enlarged chart of **NVIDIA Corp** [(NASDAQ:NVDA)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA).

Note the following:

- This article is about the big picture, not an individual stock. The chart of NVDA stock is being used to illustrate the point. Nvidia earnings, along with **Anthropic’s** (ANT) IPO, President Trump’s visit to Asia, FOMC minutes, positioning, money flows, sentiment, and technicals, are the most important elements driving the stock market at this time.
- The chart shows that NVDA stock has risen after earnings.
- The chart shows that in spite of very strong earnings and guidance, the [bulls’ hopium](https://www.benzinga.com/opinion/26/11/63352031/nvidia-earnings-first-without-huang-options-market-signals-8-5-stock-move) did not come true.
- The chart shows that the bears’ hopium also did not come true.
- It is worth a reminder that hopium is not a good investment strategy.
- In our analysis, based on earnings and guidance alone, NVDA stock should have been up 15% – 20% this morning.
- Wall Street is almost unanimously very bullish after earnings.
- In our analysis, the reason for the subdued stock market reaction is the unanswered questions.
- **In our analysis, NVDA appears to be putting a floor under NVDA stock by stepping up buybacks.** NVDA bought back \$22.1 billion of stock last quarter and plans to spend another \$227.3 billion by the end of fiscal 2028. This works out to about \$45 billion per quarter over the next five quarters, more than double the latest quarter. Such large buybacks could help support NVDA stock.
- In yesterday’s Morning Capsule, we gave you eight questions to focus on during NVDA’s earnings and conference call. Here are the answers.
  - Will NVDA beat expectations? Yes. Revenue was \$115.8 billion versus \$109 billion expected. Adjusted EPS was \$2.68 versus \$2.48 expected. Whisper numbers were higher than consensus. NVDA beat the whisper numbers.
  - How will NVDA guidance measure up to expectations? NVDA guided to \$130 billion in fourth quarter revenue versus about \$125 billion expected. Fiscal 2028 revenue growth guidance was raised from 70% to 75%.
  - **How much NVDA revenue is at risk from China? Our most important question went unanswered. NVDA disclosed \$2.4 billion in Hopper chip sales to China. NVDA interim CEO Colette Kress said that China revenue was about 10%. However, in our analysis, this is misleading, as a significant portion of the revenue comes indirectly from China through customers in other countries. We previously estimated that direct and indirect China revenue is in the range of 12% – 20% of NVDA sales.**
  - Can NVDA maintain its extraordinary gross margins? Gross margins were 74.9%. NVDA expects 71% – 72% next quarter and 72% – 73% in fiscal 2028. Both are below the latest reported level.
  - Is the Vera Rubin rollout on track? Yes. NVDA reported nearly \$20 billion in first quarter production shipments, its fastest ramp ever.
  - Are hyperscalers still spending aggressively on AI? Yes. Hyperscaler revenue rose 23% to \$60.1 billion. Demand still exceeds supply.
  - How much of NVDA’s growth depends on financing customers and investing in companies that buy its chips? NVDA disclosed \$118 billion in maximum guarantee exposure and \$32 billion in future neocloud commitments. **What we still do not know is how much revenue depends on NVDA’s financial support of its customers.**
  - What will management say about finding a permanent CEO? The board is considering internal and external candidates and does not plan to bring Jensen Huang back. **We still do not know if NVDA can maintain its technology lead without Huang.**
- **Our second most important question was about gross margins. After earnings, Wall Street does not appear to be concerned. In our analysis, Wall Street may be missing the gross margin risk.** Here are the key points:
  - Wall Street was pleased with NVDA’s earnings and guidance. However, analysts did not ask how losing China linked customers could affect future gross margins.
  - The Trump administration is tightening restrictions on Chinese companies accessing American AI computing through data centers in other countries. NVDA has also formed a new board committee to oversee export controls.
  - Yesterday, we shared our analysis that direct and indirect China related sales may account for 12% – 20% of NVDA revenue. NVDA did not disclose enough to determine how close our estimate is to the actual number.
  - There are plenty of buyers for NVDA chips. Even if NVDA loses China-linked customers, it may be able to sell those chips elsewhere without much impact on revenue.
  - **Here is what Wall Street may be missing. Losing China-linked customers could leave NVDA more dependent on a few very large hyperscalers. These customers may gain bargaining power and negotiate lower prices, hurting gross margins.**
  - NVDA is guiding to 72% – 73% gross margins for fiscal 2028. This guidance was first issued before the latest China restrictions and was reaffirmed yesterday. It remains to be seen whether NVDA can meet this guidance if it loses more China-linked business.
- **In our analysis, NVDA may be able to replace China-linked sales, but not necessarily at the same gross margins. The risk may become more significant in fiscal 2029 as large customers gain bargaining power and alternatives to NVDA chips improve.**
- For the very short term, continue to watch smart money flows and momo crowd money flows. Strong earnings do not settle the bigger questions about China, gross margins, and NVDA’s future without Jensen Huang.
  - In the early trade, momo crowd money flows are very positive in NVDA.
  - In the early trade, smart money flows are very positive in NVDA.
- As a full disclosure, on our long core NVDA position from \$12.55, partial profits have been taken.
- Demand for Anthropic (ANT) appears to be strong. The IPO will be priced tonight, and ANT will start trading tomorrow.
- President Trump has arrived in China for the APEC summit. President Xi personally welcomed him at the airport. Trump is expected to meet with Xi and Russian President Putin on Thursday, with trade, Ukraine, and nuclear weapons among the topics.
- **In our analysis, a big issue for investors is whether Trump and Xi can make progress on AI chips and trade, especially with China threatening to retaliate against the latest U.S. export restrictions.**

 

- FOMC minutes will be released at 2 pm ET and may be market moving.

#### **Housing**

The housing picture is mixed. Here are the details:

- Housing starts came in at 1.30M vs 1.25M consensus
- Housing permits came in at 1.295M vs 1.377M consensus

#### **Magnificent Seven Money Flows**

Most portfolios are now heavily concentrated in the Mag 7 stocks.  For this reason, it is important to pay attention to early money flows in the Mag 7 stocks on a daily basis.

In the early trade, money flows are positive in Nvidia (NVDA) and **Tesla Inc** [(NASDAQ:TSLA)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TSLA).

In the early trade, money flows are neutral in **Amazon.com, Inc.** [(NASDAQ:AMZN)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AMZN).

In the early trade, money flows are negative in **Apple Inc** [(NASDAQ:AAPL)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/AAPL), **Alphabet Inc Class C** [(NASDAQ:GOOG)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/GOOG), **Meta Platforms Inc** [(NASDAQ:META)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/META), and **Microsoft Corp** [(NASDAQ:MSFT)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MSFT).

In the early trade, money flows are positive in **SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust** [(NYSE:SPY)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SPY) and **Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1** [(NASDAQ:QQQ)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/QQQ).

#### **Momo Crowd And Smart Money In Stocks**

Investors can gain an edge by knowing money flows in SPY and QQQ.  Investors can get a bigger edge by knowing when smart money is buying stocks, gold, and oil.  The most popular ETF for gold is **SPDR Gold Trust** (GLD).  The most popular ETF for silver is **iShares Silver Trust** (SLV).  The most popular ETF for oil is **United States Oil ETF** (USO).

#### **Bitcoin**

**Bitcoin** [(CRYPTO: BTC)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BTC-USD) is rangebound.

# Novo Nordisk Showcases CagriSema Trial Gains and Wegovy Food Noise Reductions Ahead of FDA Decision

**Novo Nordisk** [(NYSE:NVO)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVO) presented trial and real-world data at ObesityWeek 2026 showing strong weight loss for investigational CagriSema and reduced food noise among Wegovy users.

**Read Also: [Novo Nordisk Scores EU Win For Hemophilia Drug, Advances Sickle Cell Treatment Toward Approval](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/biotech/26/11/63257974/novo-nordisk-scores-eu-win-for-hemophilia-drug-advances-sickle-cell-treatment-toward-approval)**

## CagriSema Delivers Weight Loss Across Lower Doses

On Saturday, Novo Nordisk [unveiled](https://www.novonordisk.com/content/nncorp/global/en/news-and-media/news-and-ir-materials/news-details.html?id=920561) primary Phase 3 REDEFINE 9 results in Washington, D.C., alongside simultaneous publication in *The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology*.

The trial tested CagriSema, a fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide and semaglutide, at doses below its 2.4 mg / 2.4 mg maximum.

Assuming full adherence, adults taking the 1.7 mg / 1.7 mg and 1.0 mg / 1.0 mg doses achieved 20.7% and 21.0% average [weight loss](https://www.benzinga.com/topic/weight-loss) at week 68, versus 2.0% for placebo. They also cut waist circumference by 17.2 cm and 17.5 cm, respectively, compared with 3.6 cm for placebo.

Under the treatment regimen estimand, those doses produced 19.4% and 18.6% weight loss versus 4.6% for placebo.

## Early Responders and Quality-of-Life Gains

On Sunday, the company [shared](https://www.novonordisk.com/content/nncorp/global/en/news-and-media/news-and-ir-materials/news-details.html?id=920645) two post hoc analyses from the Phase 3 REDEFINE 1 trial of CagriSema 2.4 mg / 2.4 mg. About 67.8% of treated participants lost at least 5% of their body weight by week 8 and reached 25.4% mean weight loss at week 68, versus [17.8% for delayed responders](https://www.benzinga.com/general/health-care).

At week 68, 73.1% reported meaningful physical function gains and 69.0% reported psychosocial improvements, topping placebo rates of 49.1% and 42.1%.

Novo Nordisk filed a New Drug Application with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in December 2025 for CagriSema 2.4 mg / 2.4 mg and expects a decision in the fourth quarter of 2026.

U.S. regulators have not approved CagriSema, and trials have not established its safety and efficacy.

## Wegovy Reduces Food Noise in Real-World Studies

Novo Nordisk also [presented](https://www.novonordisk.com/content/nncorp/global/en/news-and-media/news-and-ir-materials/news-details.html?id=920563) Saturday findings from the retrospective SIGNAL and OCTANE studies using de-identified Ro telehealth data and a seven-item questionnaire tracking intrusive food thoughts.

In SIGNAL, 26,213 adults initiating [semaglutide injections](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/11/62863179/novo-nordisk-raises-2026-outlook-as-wegovy-pill-shines) cut food-noise scores from a 2.72 baseline by 0.42 points at one month and 0.72 points at six months.

In OCTANE, adults starting oral semaglutide lowered food-noise scores by roughly 25% over three months, while 86.4% reported at least one improvement, including better-fitting clothing (67.5%) and [healthier eating (51.6%)](https://www.benzinga.com/general/biotech).

# Novo Nordisk Raises 2026 Outlook As Wegovy Pill Shines

**Novo Nordisk A/S** [(NYSE:](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVO)[NVO](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVO)) stock rose Wednesday after the drugmaker reported better-than-expected third-quarter earnings and raised its full-year outlook.

## Novo Nordisk’s Obesity Sales Jump 22%

The weight loss drugmaker reported third-quarter sales of \$11.90 billion (79.195 billion Danish kroner), beating Wall Street’s estimate of \$11.39 billion.

Sales rose 4% at constant exchange rates (CER), driven by strong demand for GLP-1 drugs, particularly obesity treatments.

Obesity [sales](https://www.novonordisk.com/news-and-media/news-and-ir-materials/news-details.html?id=919765) jumped 22% at CER to 26.146 billion kroner. Higher sales volumes across markets fueled the growth.

However, diabetes sales fell 5% at CER to 47.545 billion kroner.

U.S. GLP-1 diabetes sales declined 10% at CER due to lower volumes and changes in wholesaler inventories.

Injectable Ozempic sales fell 11% at CER, while oral semaglutide sales under the Rybelsus brand rose 5%.

Weekly new-to-brand prescriptions for the Ozempic pill are now about 100% higher than pre-launch levels under the Rybelsus brand.

## Novo Nordisk’s Operating Profit Jumps 27%

Adjusted operating profit climbed 27% at CER to 31.720 billion kroner.

GLP-1 sales growth and lower year-over-year transformation expenses supported profitability.

The company recorded about 9 billion kroner in transformation costs a year earlier. However, roughly 3.5 billion kroner in one-time expenses partly offset the latest quarter’s gains.

Novo Nordisk reported adjusted earnings of 87 cents per share (5.79 kroner), beating analysts’ [estimate of 81 cents](https://www.benzinga.com/earnings).

**See More: [Top Value Stocks](https://www.benzinga.com/screener/top-value-stocks)**

## Wegovy Pill Sets U.S. Launch Record

Wegovy pill prescriptions reached about 3.6 million during the quarter, bringing the total to more than 8 million since launch.

The company described it as the strongest GLP-1 volume launch in U.S. history.

The pill generated 4.178 billion kroner in U.S. sales during the quarter.

Meanwhile, injectable Wegovy [sales](https://ml-eu.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/8d56aec0-b469-4180-81ee-3c3c000beca2) reached 20.407 billion kroner, down 2% at CER.

Total Wegovy pill sales reached 5.394 billion kroner, while Ozempic sales fell 5% to 29.706 billion kroner.

Wegovy pill sales surged 53% from the previous quarter, beating the 4.62 billion kroner consensus estimate, Reuters reported.

CEO **Mike Doustdar** told Reuters that Novo has held its ground since Eli Lilly launched its rival pill. Investors said Novo leads in oral obesity treatments, while Lilly dominates the injectable market. However, they warned that competition could intensify.

## Novo Nordisk Raises 2026 Outlook

Novo Nordisk raised its 2026 forecast, citing stronger expectations [for GLP-1 sales](https://www.benzinga.com/calendars/guidance).

The company now expects adjusted sales growth and adjusted operating profit growth of negative 2% to positive 2% at CER.

Its previous forecast called for [declines of up to 6%](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/08/60924329/ozempic-maker-novo-nordisk-raises-outlook-but-sales-fall-on-tough-comparison-stock-tanks).

# Bitcoin Sank Ahead of SpaceX's IPO. Now It's Falling Before Anthropic's — But for a Different Reason

Five months ago, bitcoin fell ahead of SpaceX’s listing. Whether crypto had to pay the bill for the IPO is less clear.

**Bitcoin** [(CRYPTO: BTC)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BTC-USD) fell 19% in the 50 days before SpaceX began trading in June, and it is down 23% over the past 50 days ahead of Anthropic’s debut, according to Block Scholes, an institutional crypto derivatives data firm.

But the actors have swapped roles.

In June, AI stocks were booming while crypto bled. This time, AI is leading the selloff.

Bitcoin traded near \$63,940 at 3:30 p.m. ET Tuesday, down 1.4% and about 26% below its Oct. 4 close of \$86,475.

**Anthropic PBC** is expected to price its IPO on Wednesday, with shares set to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The AI developer has set a range of \$70 to \$78 per share.

So is Anthropic draining money out of crypto? Or is something bigger at work?

## **Two Slides, Almost Identical**

On the chart, the two declines look like twins. Bitcoin fell 22.4% from its mid-May peak into SpaceX’s debut, and it has dropped 21.3% from its Nov. 4 high ahead of Anthropic’s.

![Bitcoin daily chart, drawdowns ahead of SpaceX and Anthropic IPOs](https://editorial-assets.benzinga.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/17142933/bitcoin-spacex-anthropic-tradingview.png)

*Bitcoin daily chart, with the drawdowns ahead of the SpaceX and Anthropic listings. Source: TradingView*

The backdrop is the opposite.

Before SpaceX, the Nasdaq-100 rose 11% and **Nvidia Corp.** [(NASDAQ:NVDA)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA) gained 3%. This time, Nvidia is down 32% and the Nasdaq-100 is 11% lower over the same window, according to Block Scholes.

“This time, the sell-off has been led by the AI trade itself,” Thahbib Rahman, research analyst at Block Scholes, said in an emailed note Tuesday.

**Read Also: [Dow Slides 1.4% as Salesforce Leads Software Rout Before Anthropic IPO: Stock Market Today](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/11/63359152/stock-market-today-salesforce-software-selloff-anthropic-ipo-nvidia-november-17)**

## **Bitcoin Now Moves With Nvidia, Not Gold**

Bitcoin’s 30-day correlation with Nvidia has climbed from 0.20 at the end of September to 0.56, while its correlation with gold has fallen from 0.63 to 0.39, Block Scholes said.

Earlier this year, bitcoin’s link to gold hit multi-year highs.

“That relationship is weakening and liquidity is ebbing and flowing out of crypto and equities together once more,” Rahman said.

Spot bitcoin ETFs have seen \$3.0 billion in net outflows in the run-up to the Anthropic listing, according to Block Scholes. The **iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF** [(NASDAQ:IBIT)](https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IBIT) has recorded 11 straight sessions of outflows.

![iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF daily chart with fund flows ahead of the SpaceX and Anthropic listings](https://editorial-assets.benzinga.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/17143736/image-360-1024x756.png)

*IBIT ETF daily chart and fund flows, with the drawdowns ahead of the SpaceX and Anthropic listings. Source: TradingView*

## **The Anthropic Theory Has Its Skeptics**

“The Anthropic theory rests on the 20 percent selloff before the SpaceX IPO, but that came at the peak of AI bullishness, the market is through that, and the Anthropic valuation has been falling,” **Jesse Marre**, senior portfolio manager at Hilbert Group, said in emailed comments Monday.

Marre blamed a weekend flush in leveraged positions instead.

“It is much more likely this was simply a stop loss run, and the entire perp market has now basically capitulated,” Marre said.

Marre also cited a hot inflation report that pushed odds of a December Federal Reserve hike to about 90%.

HSBC sees the listing as a possible turning point.

“This week’s Anthropic IPO could well be the next bullish catalyst for tech given likely more reasonable valuations,” Max Kettner, chief multi-asset strategist at HSBC, said in a note Monday.

“We also think it’s very unlikely that even a successful IPO will finally lead to a more ‘trending’ market,” Kettner said.

**Read Also: [Jensen Huang Became AI's Insurer of Last Resort: Can Nvidia Now Fulfill a \$400 Billion Promise?](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/11/63350356/nvidia-400-billion-commitments-jensen-huang-neoclouds)**

## **What Happened After SpaceX**

Bitcoin bottomed 18 days after SpaceX’s listing, closing near \$58,600 on July 1, and was back above its starting level within 100 days.

However, the trigger came from Washington. On Aug. 19, the Treasury announced larger buybacks of longer-dated debt, and bitcoin jumped from about \$64,700 to \$78,300 in three sessions.

“That rebound had a clear catalyst of its own, which makes it hard to attribute to capital flowing back from SpaceX,” Rahman said.

This time, no buyback is on the calendar. Instead, there is an Nvidia earnings report, the year’s second blockbuster IPO and a Fed that markets now expect to hike.

result.question: By March 31, 2027
result.rules:
This market will settle to Yes if the United States and Iran sign or formally adopt a written diplomatic instrument that qualifies as a nuclear deal under the provision below, by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET. Outcome sourced from the United States, Iran, and the officially released text of the instrument.

A diplomatic instrument will qualify as a nuclear deal if it establishes at least one specific obligation limiting Iran's nuclear program through a concrete, measurable benchmark against which compliance could be tested, which may take the form of a defined limit, prohibition, or quantity (e.g., a specific cap on the purity level to which Iran may enrich uranium, or an explicit commitment for Iran to surrender, destroy, or dilute its enriched uranium stockpile). Non-specific or vague restrictions, with no defined metric (e.g., a pledge not to pursue nuclear weapons, a commitment to maintain the status quo, or an agreement to abide IAEA monitoring or inspections requirements that do not specifically restrict Iran's nuclear program) will not qualify.

The content of the qualifying instrument must be expressed as an agreed obligation to be implemented. The following do not qualify: (i) a provision the substantive obligation of which remains explicitly subject to a future agreement, negotiation process, or mutually agreed follow-on instrument; (ii) a provision explicitly framed as a minimum requirement for a future negotiation, rather than a present obligation; (iii) a floor, placeholder, or minimum standard established explicitly for the purpose of structuring ongoing or future talks.

A definite and unconditional obligation may qualify, even if technical or procedural details, including the exact implementation date, timeframe, or sequencing, remain subject to future arrangements, provided that the obligation still establishes a concrete, measurable benchmark against which compliance could be tested. Conditional obligations do not qualify.

Unless the written instrument is formally adopted without signature as described below, the instrument must be signed by both the United States and Iran. Both parties must either sign the same document or sign individual documents that substantively and directly indicate acceptance of the same underlying instrument, regardless of minor formatting, wording, or translation differences between the signed versions. Both physical signatures and officially-issued electronic signatures will qualify as signatures.

If the written instrument is recognized by the United States and Iran as not requiring signature for execution, formal adoption of the instrument by both countries without signature will qualify. Formal adoption may be established by official actions, including: (i) an official joint statement announcing that the United States and Iran have adopted, approved, executed, concluded, or otherwise finalized the instrument; (ii) mutual official confirmation that the same published instrument has been agreed to, adopted, approved, executed, or concluded by both countries; (iii) adoption, approval, or endorsement through an official resolution, ministerial decision, executive decision, or equivalent institutional act, where that act is the mechanism by which the relevant country adopts the instrument; or (iv) an exchange of official diplomatic notes or letters confirming acceptance of the same instrument.

Whether an instrument qualifies will be primarily determined by its officially released text. A qualifying instrument must be signed or formally adopted by both the United States and Iran by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. If such an instrument is signed or formally adopted by that time, but the complete text has not been released within 28 days of adoption, official and definitive announcements from the United States and Iran regarding the text, or a consensus of major news agencies of record, may be used to determine whether the instrument qualifies. If, on March 31, 2027, the text of such an instrument has not been released and genuine material ambiguity remains as to whether it satisfies this market's requirements, settlement may be postponed to allow for 28 calendar days after the date of adoption to pass pending release of the text.

Once a diplomatic instrument has been signed or formally adopted without signature by both the United States and Iran and confirmed to satisfy the requirements of a qualifying written diplomatic instrument, this market's condition is met, regardless of whether the instrument later enters into force, is ratified, receives legislative or treaty consent, or is subsequently repudiated, withdrawn from, or not implemented by the United States or Iran.

result.question: Will the US agree to a new Iranian nuclear deal this year?
result.rules:
If the United States has agreed to, signed, or accepted a new Iran-US nuclear deal before Jul 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.

An agreement also made with other countries (i.e. multilaterally) is still encompassed if the United States participates. "A new Iran-US nuclear deal" means a formal written agreement signed by authorized representatives of both the United States and Iran that (1) imposes verifiable restrictions on Iran's nuclear program, including limits on uranium enrichment, centrifuge numbers, or nuclear facility operations, AND (2) provides for the lifting, suspension, or modification of at least one US economic sanction on Iran in exchange for Iran's nuclear commitments.

Clarification (04/19/26): The Agreement Long rulebook variable defines the nature of the qualifying instrument: it must be a formal written agreement signed by authorized representatives of both governments. It does not impose a precondition that the signing itself must occur before resolution. Because the Payout Criterion is satisfied if the United States has "agreed to, signed, or accepted" such an instrument, both governments publicly and officially agreeing to the terms of what will be a qualifying written agreement is sufficient to resolve the market to Yes, even if the formal signing has not yet taken place.

Clarification (06/02/26): A qualifying instrument must impose "verifiable restrictions on Iran's nuclear program." A restriction is "verifiable" only where it establishes a concrete, objectively ascertainable standard (a defined limit, prohibition, quantity, or monitoring provision) against which compliance could in principle be confirmed; a general expression of intent that fixes no such standard is not considered “verifiable” for the purposes of this event. Accordingly, a bare pledge not to develop or pursue nuclear weapons, unaccompanied by any concrete limit on Iran's nuclear materials, activities, or facilities, does not on its own satisfy criterion (1). Conversely, a commitment to completely 'stop' or ‘suspend’ a specific nuclear activity (such as uranium enrichment) establishes a concrete prohibition (an implicit limit of zero) and qualifies as a restriction, whereas a vague promise to 'reduce' activities without a defined metric or monitoring mechanism does not. The enumerated examples (limits on uranium enrichment, centrifuge numbers, or nuclear facility operations) are illustrative and not exhaustive: a formal, verifiable commitment to remove, transfer, or cap Iran's stock of enriched uranium, confirmable by the receiving state or an oversight body, is a restriction on Iran's nuclear program and satisfies criterion (1). In every case, criterion (2) must independently be met.

Clarification (06/17/26): To clarify, the U.S.–Iran memorandum of understanding reportedly now in effect does not satisfy criterion (1) of the definition of a "new Iran-US nuclear deal," and this market will therefore not resolve to Yes on the basis of that instrument at this time. The memorandum provides for the existing state of Iran's nuclear program to be maintained pending a subsequent agreement, and defers the disposition of Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium to a mechanism to be mutually agreed in that subsequent agreement. That it states a minimum methodology for that future mechanism — down-blending on site under IAEA supervision — constrains the form of a mechanism yet to be agreed, but specifies no quantity, enrichment level, or completion deadline for the down-blending. An instrument that provides for maintaining Iran's nuclear program at an unspecified status quo, or that defers its substantive nuclear commitments to a subsequent agreement, does not by itself establish the concrete, objectively ascertainable standard that a "verifiable" restriction requires.

result.question: Will Jensen Huang rejoin NVIDIA by December 31, 2027?
result.rules:
On November 12, 2026, NVIDIA announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as its President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of its Board of Directors, effective immediately.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Jensen Huang is officially announced as accepting or beginning a formal role within the corporate or governance structure of NVIDIA between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

Qualifying roles include employment, executive, officer, director, formal advisory, or governance positions at NVIDIA, including on an interim or acting basis and membership in a body formally responsible for governing or overseeing the company. A role within a subsidiary or controlled entity of NVIDIA will also qualify.

Merely holding or trading NVIDIA shares, voting as a shareholder, entering into a commercial or research partnership with NVIDIA, informally advising, appearing at NVIDIA events, or receiving an honorary or emeritus title will not qualify unless Jensen Huang also accepts or begins a formal role within NVIDIA’s corporate or governance structure.

An official announcement that Jensen Huang has accepted a qualifying role will be sufficient, regardless of when he formally begins serving in that role.

The primary resolution source will be official information from NVIDIA (including its filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission) or Jensen Huang; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
