result.question: Will the US and China agree to or announce another extension of the Busan trade truce before Jan 11, 2027?
result.rules:
If the US and China agree to or announce another extension of the Busan trade truce before Jan 11, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.

Another extension means that, after Issuance, both governments announce that the Busan trade truce will continue past Jan 10, 2027. It must cover China's suspension of its additional 24% tariff on US goods and the US suspension of port fees on China-linked ships, which are now due to expire on Jan 10, 2027, or be a statement that the truce as a whole is extended. A longer-lasting trade arrangement that replaces them also qualifies.

A joint statement qualifies, as do separate official statements or notices from each government. An announcement by one government qualifies only if the other government also confirms it, and counts from the date of that confirmation. An extension announced by only one government, an extension of other measures only, and an agreement on purchases or tariff cuts that leaves those suspensions to expire do NOT qualify. Extensions announced before Issuance, including the two-month extension to Jan 10, 2027, do NOT count.

An agreement or announcement qualifies if it involves any of the following:

Formal signing of treaties
Parliamentary approval with binding effect
Official ratification
Formal commitment by the head of state/government with constitutional authority
Official statements by authorized ministers
Official press releases
Formal declarations during government proceedings
Official statements to international bodies

Phased implementation announcements and multi-party agreements where the country is a signatory also qualify.

The following do NOT qualify:

Preliminary discussions
Conditional agreements contingent on circumstances
Opposition party statements
Leaked documents
Think-tank recommendations
General aspirations without specific commitment
Draft legislation without approval
Regional actions (unless specified)
Retraction of previously announced commitments

He noted that Apple raised iPhone prices by about \$100, less than the roughly \$200 increase some had expected.

Mohan sees the margin pressure as a near-term challenge but believes higher pricing could eventually support profitability once memory costs normalize, particularly across future iPhone replacement cycles.

He also supported Apple’s decision to build inventory and secure longer-term memory contracts as hyperscalers increasingly compete for the same components.

The key uncertainty, he said, is whether higher prices eventually weaken consumer demand.

## T. Rowe Price Sees Market-Share Gains

He believes lower memory prices could eventually provide an additional margin tailwind while Apple continues expanding its installed base and ecosystem.

Wang also cautioned that memory remains a cyclical industry and said sufficiently high prices could eventually hurt demand or push customers to redesign products around expensive components.

Still, he said Apple’s ability to preserve shipments and navigate higher input costs supports its longer-term growth prospects.

I'm setting the consequences on the event and on the half-point way: a +1.2% equity move with a slight rise in long yields and a weaker dollar when no hike happens, against a -2% equity drop, higher yields, a stronger dollar, and a -0.6% hit to bonds if the half-point hike lands. I'm setting the hold case as the mirror of the hike: front-end yields falling about 15bp, the S&P up roughly 0.8%, the dollar down 0.8%, and bonds up around 0.4%, with long yields roughly flat since some inflation-risk premium might offset the relief. to.text: The FOMC raises the federal funds target range by 50 basis points or more, to 4.25%-4.50% or higher, at the meeting ending December 9, 2026. Governor Waller is the only official to back it publicly; New York Fed President Williams has ruled it out.

shock.note: A half-point move against 6-7% priced would lift front-end yields by roughly 15-20bp and signal a faster path. On Nov 10, 2026, when hot CPI moved the 2-year 17bp, the S&P 500 lost 0.4% in a day; a surprise at the meeting itself, with Waller's 'shock' framing, is larger. I put the S&P 1.5% below where a quarter point leaves it.
On Nov 10 the 10-year rose 10bp for a 17bp move in the 2-year (CNN, 'Bond yields surge most in 19 months'); hawkish Fed news this month has flattened the curve, so I carry about 6bp to the long end.
A wider rate gap extends the dollar's rally; the dollar index is already at a 19-month high on hike expectations, so the further move is modest.
BND's duration is near 6 and its yields sit in the 2- to 10-year part of the curve, which moves more than the long end on a policy surprise: about 12bp there is -0.7%.

A hold, priced at about 3%, removes roughly 15bp from front-end yields. Relief for equities is tempered because a Fed that holds with core inflation running 3.5-3.7% annualised invites doubt about inflation control. I put the S&P 0.8% above the quarter-point baseline.
Lower policy-rate expectations pull long yields down while a larger inflation-risk premium pushes them up; I take the two to cancel at the long end.

markets.question: Will the Fed hike-hike-hike in the next three decisions (Dec-Jan-Mar)?
markets.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds rate. The decisions on the target federal funds rate are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 8 to 9, 2026; January 26 to 27, 2027; and March 16 to 17, 2027.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate moves are explicitly excluded from this market. Any hike or cut to the target federal funds rate announced outside the three regularly scheduled meetings listed above, including at any unscheduled or emergency FOMC meeting, will not be considered and will not count as one of the three decisions. Each scheduled meeting's decision is measured against the upper bound in effect immediately before that meeting, including any emergency change made since the previous meeting, regardless of whether the scheduled decision reverses an emergency change.

https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

markets.question: Will the US agree to a new Iranian nuclear deal this year?
markets.rules:
If the United States has agreed to, signed, or accepted a new Iran-US nuclear deal before Jul 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.

An agreement also made with other countries (i.e. multilaterally) is still encompassed if the United States participates. "A new Iran-US nuclear deal" means a formal written agreement signed by authorized representatives of both the United States and Iran that (1) imposes verifiable restrictions on Iran's nuclear program, including limits on uranium enrichment, centrifuge numbers, or nuclear facility operations, AND (2) provides for the lifting, suspension, or modification of at least one US economic sanction on Iran in exchange for Iran's nuclear commitments.

Clarification (04/19/26): The Agreement Long rulebook variable defines the nature of the qualifying instrument: it must be a formal written agreement signed by authorized representatives of both governments. It does not impose a precondition that the signing itself must occur before resolution. Because the Payout Criterion is satisfied if the United States has "agreed to, signed, or accepted" such an instrument, both governments publicly and officially agreeing to the terms of what will be a qualifying written agreement is sufficient to resolve the market to Yes, even if the formal signing has not yet taken place.

Clarification (06/02/26): A qualifying instrument must impose "verifiable restrictions on Iran's nuclear program." A restriction is "verifiable" only where it establishes a concrete, objectively ascertainable standard (a defined limit, prohibition, quantity, or monitoring provision) against which compliance could in principle be confirmed; a general expression of intent that fixes no such standard is not considered “verifiable” for the purposes of this event. Accordingly, a bare pledge not to develop or pursue nuclear weapons, unaccompanied by any concrete limit on Iran's nuclear materials, activities, or facilities, does not on its own satisfy criterion (1). Conversely, a commitment to completely 'stop' or ‘suspend’ a specific nuclear activity (such as uranium enrichment) establishes a concrete prohibition (an implicit limit of zero) and qualifies as a restriction, whereas a vague promise to 'reduce' activities without a defined metric or monitoring mechanism does not. The enumerated examples (limits on uranium enrichment, centrifuge numbers, or nuclear facility operations) are illustrative and not exhaustive: a formal, verifiable commitment to remove, transfer, or cap Iran's stock of enriched uranium, confirmable by the receiving state or an oversight body, is a restriction on Iran's nuclear program and satisfies criterion (1). In every case, criterion (2) must independently be met.

Clarification (06/17/26): To clarify, the U.S.–Iran memorandum of understanding reportedly now in effect does not satisfy criterion (1) of the definition of a "new Iran-US nuclear deal," and this market will therefore not resolve to Yes on the basis of that instrument at this time. The memorandum provides for the existing state of Iran's nuclear program to be maintained pending a subsequent agreement, and defers the disposition of Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium to a mechanism to be mutually agreed in that subsequent agreement. That it states a minimum methodology for that future mechanism — down-blending on site under IAEA supervision — constrains the form of a mechanism yet to be agreed, but specifies no quantity, enrichment level, or completion deadline for the down-blending. An instrument that provides for maintaining Iran's nuclear program at an unspecified status quo, or that defers its substantive nuclear commitments to a subsequent agreement, does not by itself establish the concrete, objectively ascertainable standard that a "verifiable" restriction requires.

markets.question: Will the US and China agree to or announce another extension of the Busan trade truce before Jan 11, 2027?
markets.family: Will the US and China extend their trade truce again?
markets.rules:
If the US and China agree to or announce another extension of the Busan trade truce before Jan 11, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.

Another extension means that, after Issuance, both governments announce that the Busan trade truce will continue past Jan 10, 2027. It must cover China's suspension of its additional 24% tariff on US goods and the US suspension of port fees on China-linked ships, which are now due to expire on Jan 10, 2027, or be a statement that the truce as a whole is extended. A longer-lasting trade arrangement that replaces them also qualifies.

A joint statement qualifies, as do separate official statements or notices from each government. An announcement by one government qualifies only if the other government also confirms it, and counts from the date of that confirmation. An extension announced by only one government, an extension of other measures only, and an agreement on purchases or tariff cuts that leaves those suspensions to expire do NOT qualify. Extensions announced before Issuance, including the two-month extension to Jan 10, 2027, do NOT count.

An agreement or announcement qualifies if it involves any of the following:

Formal signing of treaties
Parliamentary approval with binding effect
Official ratification
Formal commitment by the head of state/government with constitutional authority
Official statements by authorized ministers
Official press releases
Formal declarations during government proceedings
Official statements to international bodies

Phased implementation announcements and multi-party agreements where the country is a signatory also qualify.

The following do NOT qualify:

Preliminary discussions
Conditional agreements contingent on circumstances
Opposition party statements
Leaked documents
Think-tank recommendations
General aspirations without specific commitment
Draft legislation without approval
Regional actions (unless specified)
Retraction of previously announced commitments
markets.resolution_source: The White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/); Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (https://ustr.gov/); U.S. Department of the Treasury (https://home.treasury.gov/); Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China (https://english.mofcom.gov.cn/); The State Council of the People's Republic of China (https://english.www.gov.cn/); Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/); the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/)

markets.question: Will the FDA approve CagriSema before Jan 1, 2027?
markets.rules:
If the FDA approves CagriSema for marketing before Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.

An approval is defined as:

For new drugs: FDA issuance of an approval letter for a New Drug Application (NDA) or Biologics License Application (BLA)
For already-marketed drugs seeking new indications: FDA approval of a supplemental NDA (sNDA) or supplemental BLA (sBLA) for the specific indication referenced
For generic drugs: FDA approval of an Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA)
For biosimilars: FDA approval of a 351(k) application

The following constitute approvals that trigger the Payout Criterion:

Standard approval (traditional approval based on clinical benefit)
Accelerated approval (based on surrogate endpoints)
Approval with Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS)
Approval with restricted distribution or indication limitations, except compassionate use/expanded access programs

The following do NOT constitute approvals:

Complete Response Letters (CRLs) indicating the application cannot be approved in its current form
Approvable letters that require additional actions before approval
Tentative approvals pending patent or exclusivity expiration
FDA requests for additional information or studies
Extension of Prescription Drug User Fee Amendments dates
Approval for compassionate use or expanded access programs only
Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) without full approval
Approval only for export or for use outside the United States

If the FDA issues a Complete Response Letter before Jan 1, 2027, the market will resolve to No unless the FDA subsequently approves CagriSema after addressing the CRL concerns and before Jan 1, 2027.

If the FDA convenes an Advisory Committee that votes against approval but the FDA approves CagriSema anyway before Jan 1, 2027, the market will resolve to Yes.

If CagriSema receives accelerated approval that is later withdrawn before Jan 1, 2027, the market will resolve based on whether the initial accelerated approval occurred after Issuance (Yes), regardless of the subsequent withdrawal.

If the drug sponsor withdraws the application before FDA action and before Jan 1, 2027, the market will resolve to No immediately.

result.question: Will the US government be shut down on Dec 12, 2026?
result.rules:
If the United States federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse of appropriations at 10:00 AM ET on Dec 12, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.

A shutdown is defined as the government's orderly suspension of agency work that is not legally excepted, typically accompanied by furloughing the employees who perform that work, when funding is unavailable.

Examples that would resolve the market to Yes:

OMB releases a formal directive that orders heads of the affected agencies to "execute plans for an orderly shutdown," which is in effect as of 10:00 AM ET on Dec 12, 2026
OPM posts a current operating status that indicates that "due to a partial lapse in appropriations, Federal Government operations vary by agency"

Examples that would NOT resolve the market to Yes:

A technical lapse in appropriations occurs, but OMB directs agencies to continue standard operations
Government closures or operating status changes resulting from Federal holidays, inclement weather, or other emergencies, unless such closures coincide with a shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations
result.resolution_source: Office of Management and Budget (https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/); United States Office of Personnel Management (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/)

markets.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds rate. The decisions on the target federal funds rate are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 8 to 9, 2026; January 26 to 27, 2027; and March 16 to 17, 2027.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate moves are explicitly excluded from this market. Any hike or cut to the target federal funds rate announced outside the three regularly scheduled meetings listed above, including at any unscheduled or emergency FOMC meeting, will not be considered and will not count as one of the three decisions. Each scheduled meeting's decision is measured against the upper bound in effect immediately before that meeting, including any emergency change made since the previous meeting, regardless of whether the scheduled decision reverses an emergency change.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

input.text: What I looked at and left out of the ledger, and why. (1) JPMorgan (4.1%): its own news this month is a payments outage, a vendor cyberattack with 'no disruption to our services', and a CFO handover after Q1 2027; none is sized to move the holding by more than the market does, and its rate and credit exposure is carried by the Fed rows. (3) A Ukraine settlement (Trump-Putin-Xi talks on Nov 19): lower oil would cost Exxon and help the international fund, roughly offsetting here. (4) AI regulation from the incoming Democratic Congress: the Nov 5 fall (Nasdaq -5.5%) priced the fear; with a presidential veto, law inside the horizon is unlikely, and the AI-downturn row carries the consequence if the build-out slows. (5) The run of outages at Microsoft, JPMorgan, Apple and the FAA: officials deny a coordinated attack; I found no way to put a probability on a systemic cyber event and no market that asks it. (6) A generic 'bear market' row: an index level is where the events above would show, not an event of its own, so I removed it. (1) JPMorgan (4.1%): its own news this month is a payments outage, a vendor cyberattack with 'no disruption to our services', and a CFO handover after Q1 2027; none is sized to move the holding by more than the market does, and its rate and credit exposure is carried by the Fed rows. (2) Toyota (2.7%) and the yen: USD/JPY is near 159.5 and Toyota's forecast assumes 157; a stronger yen cuts Toyota's profit but raises the dollar value of the ADR, so the net effect on this holding is small either way. (3) A Ukraine settlement (Trump-Putin-Xi talks on Nov 19): lower oil would cost Exxon and help the international fund, roughly offsetting here. (4) AI regulation from the incoming Democratic Congress: the Nov 5 fall (Nasdaq -5.5%) priced the fear; with a presidential veto, law inside the horizon is unlikely, and the AI-downturn row carries the consequence if the build-out slows. Your $504k account is about three-quarters stocks, 17% bonds, 2.4% bitcoin and the rest cash. After looking through the funds, 14.6% sits in chip stocks, with Apple at 8.3%, Microsoft at 6.9% and Nvidia at 6.7%. Over the six months to May 18, ordinary market movement alone is about ±$42,700. I built 13 events on top of that; each row is read alone, so they do not add.

**The AI build-out and Taiwan are the two largest risks**
- **AI downturn:** prop:2 is the biggest row. The Forecast is about 17%, read from Polymarket's two deadlines, and Yes costs about $36,700 (7.3%). The assumption driving it is that the S&P stands 11% lower in a recognised bust; chip stocks are already about 26% below their October peak.
- **Taiwan:** prop:4 is unlikely at about 3.6% but costs about $82,000 (16%), because TSMC, Nvidia and Apple all depend on the island. I set the Forecast below Polymarket's invasion price, which I read as an upper bound.
- **Nvidia itself:** prop:29 is the dated test after Jensen Huang's resignation; a cut costs about $4,900 and a raise adds about $2,600. prop:3 is the upside, worth about $2,300.

**Rates hit your stocks and bonds together**
- **Fed path:** prop:12 is close to a coin flip. The Worst outcome is a rate of 5% or higher (11.5%), costing about $18,200. Your bond funds do not cushion this one.
- **December meeting:** prop:1 is nearly settled; only a half-point rise (6%, about −$6,600) or a hold (3%, about +$4,300) would move you.

**Geopolitics and trade**
- **Iran:** prop:5 costs about $8,900 on Yes, with Exxon offsetting only part. A nuclear deal (about 13%) is the favourable outcome, worth about +$9,700 through cheaper oil. The 30% Forecast is my own judgement, tied to a Polymarket ceasefire contract; no market asks it directly.
- **China trade:** prop:21 costs about $11,800 on Yes; its Forecast comes from a thin Kalshi book.

**Smaller, dated rows**
- **Apple:** prop:23 is my estimate from management's warning on memory costs; about −$1,700 on Yes.
- **Microsoft:** prop:26 is also my estimate; about −$2,400 on Yes, about +$1,800 if growth tops 50%.
- **Bitcoin:** prop:7 is about ±$3,200 either way, of which roughly $2,400 is the bitcoin fund itself.
- **Novo Nordisk:** prop:6 is expected; a rejection costs about $1,200.
- **Shutdown:** prop:8 is likely to make noise but costs only about $1,300; the 43-day shutdown in 2025 did not hurt markets.

**Reading them together**
Read together, prop:2, prop:12 and prop:4 give a Volatility of about ±$21,900. In the calm case, where none of them goes wrong and the Fed stops at 4.50% (31%), you gain about $16,900. I stated three dependencies for that reading: a bust makes further Fed rises less likely, makes an Nvidia cut more likely, and a Taiwan blockade would itself trigger the bust.

**Where I am least sure**
- The sign of the stock move if the Fed stops early: it could mean cooling inflation or a cracking economy.
- Long Treasury yields in a Taiwan crisis: they rose in the April 2025 trade shock.
- The size of the S&P fall in an AI bust.
